comparison.interpretation_of_ncu: cache-control=none intentionally preserves application-managed cache state; repeat-launch cycles are therefore highly dispersed across independent NCU processes and are observational, not a point-accuracy score

interpretation: The repaired warm/cold pair uses separate first/repeat output buffers and sinks, so correctness does not overwrite the first result or hide a race. The exact binary passes host checks and compute-sanitizer memcheck, produces three fresh NVBit launches (first, eviction, repeat), and detailed replay completes all three with full coverage. The fast frontier refuses the multi-launch trace by contract. Five application-replay NCU processes with cache-control=none report the same instruction counts per launch; first-launch median is 63183 cycles, eviction median 66548, and repeat median 46876, with repeat values ranging from 46852 to 63272 because no cache flush is intentional. Launch-scope simulator lower bounds are 69383/116502/69383; stream-L2 lower bounds are 69383/116502/52557. The run demonstrates cache-scope separation and a valid multi-launch path, not a finite completion upper, point accuracy, or speedup claim.
